title: Initial amplifier semantics
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ bound the space used by $N$ on every input and every choice word. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, write $\ell(n)$ for one plus the length of the binary digit list of $n$, and set $K_*=2^{F\ell(|x|)}$. Suppose $sp(|x|)\le cS\,\ell(|x|)$, the configuration-code bound for $N,|x|,cS\,\ell(|x|)$ is at most $K_*$, and $|x|+\ell(|x|)+(cS+F)\ell(|x|)+2K_*+2\le B$. Then the amplifier started at its initial label with all registers zero terminates for every sequence of choice bits, keeps each register at most $B$ while running, and has acceptance probability equal to the run value with parameters $K_*$, $K_*+1$, and $0$.
